title: No Two Equal Letters Side by Side

concept.title: Place the most frequent letter that is not the previous one
body: Rearrange the letters of a string so that no two neighbouring letters are equal. A letter that occurs very often is the dangerous one: it needs a different letter between any two of its copies. So the greedy rule is: **at every position put the letter with the most copies left, but not the letter you just put**.

A max-heap of `(copies left, letter)` gives the most frequent letter. If the top is the previous letter, take the next one instead and put the top back afterwards. If the heap has only the previous letter left, the arrangement is impossible.

body.code:
heap = [(-count, letter) for letter, count in counts.items()]   # most copies first, then the smaller letter
heapq.heapify(heap)
result, prev = [], ""
while heap:
    count, letter = heapq.heappop(heap)
    held = None
    if letter == prev:
        if not heap:
            result = None          # only the previous letter is left
            break
        held = (count, letter)
        count, letter = heapq.heappop(heap)
    result.append(letter)
    prev = letter
    if count + 1 < 0:
        heapq.heappush(heap, (count + 1, letter))
    if held:
        heapq.heappush(heap, held)

body: The rearrangement exists exactly when the most frequent letter occurs at most `(length + 1) / 2` times (rounded down). To have a single correct answer, the rule for ties is part of the problem: among letters with the same number of copies left, the smaller letter is taken first.

statement: Rearrange the letters of `s` so that no two neighbouring letters are equal. To get exactly one answer, build the result from left to right: at every position put the letter that has the most copies left among the letters different from the previous letter, and when several letters have the same number of copies, the smallest of them. If at some position no letter other than the previous one is left, print `impossible`.
inputFormat: The first line has the string `s`.

examples.note: a (2 copies) first, then b, then a: aba.
a, b, then only a is left and it is the same as the previous letter: impossible.

hints: Count the copies of each letter and keep them in a max-heap of (count, letter).
Take the top; if it equals the previous letter, take the second one and put the first back afterwards.
If only the previous letter is left, print impossible.

explanation: A max-heap of (copies left, letter) gives the most frequent letter; if it is the previous letter the second one is used and the first is put back. If only the previous letter remains, the answer is impossible.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

s = input().strip()

import heapq
counts = {}
for c in s:
    counts[c] = counts.get(c, 0) + 1
heap = [(-v, c) for c, v in counts.items()]
heapq.heapify(heap)
result = []
prev = ""
ok = True
while heap:
    count, letter = heapq.heappop(heap)
    held = None
    if letter == prev:
        if not heap:
            ok = False
            break
        held = (count, letter)
        count, letter = heapq.heappop(heap)
    result.append(letter)
    prev = letter
    if count + 1 < 0:
        heapq.heappush(heap, (count + 1, letter))
    if held:
        heapq.heappush(heap, held)
print("".join(result) if ok else "impossible")
